value: Escalation: Alaska levies no separate late-registration penalty in AS 28.10.421 or AS 28.10.441. Instead the DMV states that 'A vehicle that has been expired for less than a full year is charged the full biennial fee beginning with the month the registration expired, even if an individual has just purchased the vehicle and the previous owner let the vehicle expire, or the vehicle has been parked while it was expired.' The registration period only starts over once the vehicle has been expired for more than a full year, or when the previous owner was fee-exempt.

value: New vehicles never titled in any state, sold by dealers who provide the buyer a Delaware Application for Title (form MV212A), are not required to be inspected. The newest seven model years of vehicles weighing 10,000 lbs or less being titled in Delaware for the first time may only be required to have a VIN verification, and 21 Del. C. § 2143(a) lets the Department waive inspection entirely for the initial registration or renewal of vehicles no older than 7 model years. Emissions testing itself applies to gasoline vehicles from model year 1968 onward (curb-idle and gas-cap test for 1968-1996; OBDII for 1996-2008 petrol and 1997-2008 diesel at 8,500 lbs MGVWR, and for any vehicle up to 14,000 lbs after 2008). A vehicle more than 25 years old branded 'reconstructed' is exempt from emissions testing but not from safety and anti-tampering inspection (21 Del. C. § 2147(a)).

value: Battery Electric: 50 · Plug In Hybrid: 0 · Hybrid: 0 · Indexed: false · Index Note: Hawaii replaced its flat EV registration surcharge with a MILEAGE-BASED ROAD USAGE CHARGE (the HiRUC program), enacted by Act 222, Session Laws of Hawaii 2023 and codified at Haw. Rev. Stat. Sec. 249-36. Timeline, precisely: (1) Until June 30, 2025, Haw. Rev. Stat. Sec. 249-31(a) imposed a flat $50 annual registration surcharge on electric vehicles AND alternative fuel vehicles. (2) Effective July 1, 2025, that $50 surcharge applies only to ALTERNATIVE FUEL VEHICLES - vehicles powered by a non-petroleum-based fuel, expressly excluding electric vehicles as defined in Sec. 249-36(g) - and electric vehicles instead become subject to the road usage charge. (3) The road usage charge is 0.8 cents per mile traveled (published by HDOT and the counties as $8 per 1,000 miles), multiplied by the miles traveled, LESS the estimated amount of paid state fuel taxes corresponding to those miles; miles are the difference between the vehicle's two most recent odometer readings as noted on the certificate of inspection under Sec. 286-26(e). The charge shall be not less than $0 and NOT MORE THAN $50 PER YEAR. (4) For the first registration renewal of a new motor vehicle for which no certificate of inspection is required, the charge assessed is $50, and that amount is subtracted from the calculation at the vehicle's second registration renewal. (5) UNTIL JUNE 30, 2028, owners of electric vehicles are offered a CHOICE to pay a flat $50 registration surcharge in lieu of the mileage-based charge; the choice is presented on the annual registration renewal notice. After June 30, 2028 the mileage-based charge applies without that opt-out. (6) HDOT must submit a long-term implementation plan for extending the road usage charge to all passenger vehicles and light duty trucks by December 31, 2033, due to the legislature no later than twenty days before the 2026 regular session. Hybrids and plug-in hybrids are expressly NOT eligible for the HiRUC program at this time and pay no EV charge. The $50 figure is a statutory cap, not indexed to any price index. · Road Usage Charge Per Mile: 0.008 · Road Usage Charge Annual Cap: 50 · Alternative Fuel Vehicle Surcharge: 50 · Program Start Date: 2025-07-01 · Flat Rate Opt Out Ends Date: 2028-06-30

value: Statewide, all motor vehicles. value: Escalation: New Hampshire publishes no dollar late fee for renewing a registration after expiry. value: Statewide, all registered vehicles. Light duty vehicles and light duty trucks up to and including 8,500 lbs GVWR take a combined Safety AND Emissions test; heavy duty vehicles and trucks over 8,500 lbs GVWR take a safety inspection only; motorcycles, trailers and semi-trailers over 1,000 lbs GVWR, and livestock trailers of any weight take a safety inspection. Fully electric light duty vehicles take the safety inspection but are exempt from emissions testing. Newly registered used vehicles must hold a valid sticker or pass inspection within 5 days of registration, and a used vehicle bought from a licensed RI dealer must have a new sticker at the time of sale (inspection no more than 90 days before the sale and no more than 500 miles accumulated since).

value: Battery Electric: 135.63 · Indexed: true · Index Note: Virginia's Highway Use Fee is recomputed by the Commissioner each July 1 and is valid July 1 - June 30. For an all-electric vehicle it is a flat annual amount ($135.63 for July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027). For every other fuel-efficient vehicle (manufacturer's combined rating of 25 MPG or greater) it is computed from the vehicle's own MPG by the statutory formula: HUF = [((11,600 average miles traveled x fuels tax rate) / 23.7) - ((11,600 average miles traveled x fuels tax rate) / vehicle's MPG rating)] x 0.85, with the current fuels tax rate of $0.326/gallon. Published values run from $7.05 at 25 MPG to $103.48 at 100 MPG for a one-year registration, and are multiplied by the number of years if registering for 2 or 3 years. A low-speed vehicle pays a flat $25. Exempt: vehicles rated under 25 MPG, autocycles, motorcycles, mopeds, vehicles over 10,000 lbs gross weight, government-owned vehicles, and IRP-registered vehicles.
